newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- up but lagging rally again.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- up but lagging rally again.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were pegged from a 1/4 to a 1/2 of a point higher at midday on Thursday, and while they were lifted by soaring Treasury bonds, municipals underperformed as trading slowed.

"Municipal cash actually is lagging everything. We've got rate-shock," a trader said. He explained that this was a typical pattern for the market, as players were waiting to see whether prices would retreat, offering them better bargains.

"This is sort of the modus operandi of the industry, they're a little slow getting out of the shoot, which doesn't make for a good trading market. Later in the day, I expect interest will pick up. Everybody is hoping that the contract will go down," the trader continued, referring to the municipal bond futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade.

For the third month in a row, U.S. retail sales fell, slipping 0.1 percent in May. The drop surprised economists polled by Reuters, who had expected a 0.4 percent increase, and this additional evidence that the economy was slowing prompted speculation that the Federal Reserve would not raise interest rates when it next meets in early July.

The positive tone in fixed-income markets was kicked off by a bigger than expected rise in weekly jobless claims. The U.S. Labor Department said weekly jobless claims rose to 339,000 for the week ended June 7.
Analysts had expected claims to drop to 326,000 after a surge to 337,000 in the prior week.
New issues on Thursday included a $55 million bond sale by the New Jersey Development Authority, which was won by Smith Barney at a true interest cost of 5.82 percent.
And Rhode Island's offering of $76 million were won by Prudential Securities, with a true interest cost of 5.180 percent.
In debt futures, the September municipal contracts rallied 25 ticks to 117-13/32. The September Treasury bond contracts also gained 25 ticks, rising to 111-12/32. The MOB spread was 193 ticks.
In the secondary market, active issues included Jefferson County, Alabama Sewer Revenues of 2027, which pay a 5-3/4 percent coupon, and were bid at 107-7/8, up two-eighths.
And Cleveland, Ohio, Certificates of Participation Cleveland Stadium Project bonds of 2027, which have a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were offered at 5.58 percent, NET, down three basis points.
